# Photos Storage 0.4.1
For Apple silicon Macs running **macOS 13 or later**. Runtime checks pass on macOS 15, 26, and 27. macOS 13 and 14 have not been runtime-tested.
- Builds for older macOS versions, including the app, helper, and System Settings pane. - Checks the installed Photos features and the meaning of its optimization setting instead of requiring one exact macOS build. - Bounds background helper checks so a stalled process cannot leave monitoring busy indefinitely. - Handles first use when Photos has not yet stored a prefetch override. - Shows an unsupported Photos version directly, without sending users to unrelated iCloud settings.
Existing iCloud Photos and Optimize Mac Storage checks remain in place; unverifiable settings stop cleanup. Photos Storage asks macOS to release eligible local copies; it does not delete items from your photo library. The storage target is approximate.
The app is Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple, with signed automatic updates. Unzip the download, move **Photos Storage.app** to **Applications**, and open it. Setup takes you to **System Settings → Photos Storage**.
If a third-party settings pane appears blank after navigating away and back, reopen Photos Storage. macOS may display a wider window for third-party panes.

# Photos Storage 0.3.1
An experimental preview for Apple silicon Macs running **macOS 27.2, build 26B123**. Cleanup is disabled on other builds.
- A new glass Photos and silver storage icon for the app and System Settings. - Matching icons at standard and Retina resolutions.
Storage targets, background monitoring, and photo safety checks work as before.
The app is signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Unzip the download, move **Photos Storage.app** to **Applications**, then open it. After permissions are granted, choose **Open System Settings** to reach **Photos Storage** directly.
The storage target is approximate. macOS decides which cached resources it can release. iCloud Photos and Optimize Mac Storage must be enabled; unknown settings stop cleanup. The app never calls a Photos asset-deletion API.
Known macOS host limitations: this third-party pane uses a wider Settings window than Apple's own panes. Navigating away and back can leave it blank; open Photos Storage again to reload it.

# Photos Storage 0.3.0
An experimental preview for Apple silicon Macs running **macOS 27.2, build 26B123**. Cleanup is disabled on other builds.
- Choose a local Photos storage target in System Settings. - See local Photos usage, with targets starting at 20 GB. - Follow guided setup for the two required permissions. - Keep monitoring active when System Settings is closed. - Receive signed automatic updates, or check manually under **Options…**.
